newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil debt levels low by int'l standards - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil debt levels low by int'l standards - cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's 268.97 billion reais in net public sector debt at end-1996 was very low in gross domestic product terms, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.
Lopes told reporters a total debt stock equivalent to 34.5 percent of GDP was low in international terms and that the average cost of the debt was not high.
Brazil's net internal public sector debt ended 1996 at 237.5 billion reais or 30.4 percent of GDP, sharply up on 1995's 170.3 billion reais or 24.5 percent of GDP.
External debt dropped to 31.5 billion reais or 4.0 percent of GDP in 1996 from 38.1 billion reais or 5.5 percent of GDP.
Lopes said the cost of the internal debt was relatively small because interest rates had steadily declined during 1996.
Nominal interest payments last year totalled 44.998 billion reais or 6.0 percent of GDP compared with 48.747 billion reais or 7.4 percent of GDP in 1995.
In real inflation-adjusted terms, interest payments dropped to 28.478 billion reais or 3.79 percent of GDP last year from 34 billion reais or 5.14 percent of GDP the year before.
